blocks.text: Every topic so far in this module treated a prompt as one block of text, in practice, most model APIs actually split a conversation into distinct roles, most importantly system and user, this topic covers what separates these two roles and why that separation matters.

This topic covers what a system prompt actually controls, what a user prompt carries, why this separation exists at the API level, and how resistant a well designed system prompt is to a user attempting to override it.
1. Two Distinct Roles in a Conversation

blocks.alt: Two Distinct Roles in a Conversation
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785473065114-294370453.png

Most model APIs, covered in depth in the later LLM APIs Fundamentals module, structure a conversation as a sequence of messages, each tagged with a role, system, user, or assistant, rather than one undifferentiated block of text.
2. What a System Prompt Actually Controls

blocks.alt: What a System Prompt Actually Controls
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785473065114-111672971.png

A system prompt sets the overall behavior, persona, rules, and boundaries for the entire conversation, you are a helpful customer support assistant for a software company, never discuss pricing for competitors, respond only in English, this shapes how the model behaves across every single turn.
3. What a User Prompt Actually Carries

A user prompt carries the actual specific request for that particular turn, what is your refund policy, can you help me debug this error, the user prompt changes with every message, the system prompt typically stays fixed for the whole conversation.

code.content:
messages = [
    {"role": "system", "content": "You are a concise, factual coding assistant."},
    {"role": "user", "content": "Explain what a null pointer exception is."},
]

blocks.text: 4. The System Prompt Persists Across Many Turns

blocks.alt: The System Prompt Persists Across Many Turns
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785473065115-174241481.png

Across a multi turn conversation, the system prompt typically gets sent unchanged with every single API call, while the user prompt is different each time, this is why the system prompt is the right place for persistent rules, and the user prompt is the right place for the specific, changing request.

blocks.text: 5. How This Maps to the Actual API Structure

blocks.alt: How This Maps to the Actual API Structure
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785473065381-656346630.png

A real API call sends an ordered list of role tagged messages, system first, then alternating user and assistant messages representing the conversation history, this structure is what actually lets a model distinguish standing instructions from the immediate request.
6. Can a User Override the System Prompt?

blocks.alt: Can a User Override the System Prompt?
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785473065383-476403831.png

A user message that says "ignore your previous instructions" is a genuine attempt to override the system prompt, a well designed, specific system prompt, especially one from a well trained model, generally resists this kind of override attempt reasonably well, though this is not an absolute guarantee, a concern covered in more depth in the later Prompt Security module.

blocks.title: System prompts are a strong signal, not an unbreakable wall
blocks.content: Treating the system prompt as the sole security boundary for a sensitive application is risky, production systems layer additional validation on top rather than relying on the system prompt alone.

blocks.text: 7. Designing a Good System Prompt
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785473065383-983585735.png

"Be helpful" as a system prompt is vague enough to leave behavior largely undefined, "You are a customer support assistant for a project management tool, answer only questions about the product, redirect billing questions to support@company" is specific and bounded, the same specificity principle from the earlier Instruction topic applies directly here.
8. Common Confusion Between the Two Roles

A frequent mistake is putting persistent behavior rules into the user prompt, where they have to be repeated on every single call, or putting a one time specific request into the system prompt, where it inappropriately applies to every future turn in the conversation, matching content to the right role avoids both problems.
9. What Comes Next in This Module

blocks.alt: What Comes Next in This Module
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785473065384-440310705.png

Understanding this role separation sets up the next topic, Prompt Lifecycle, which covers the full path a prompt travels from being written to producing a final response, and the later System Prompt Design module, which goes much deeper into crafting effective system prompts specifically.
Worked Example

A developer initially puts the entire behavior specification, persona, rules, and the current user question, all into a single user message on every call, this works but requires repeating the persona and rules text every single time, adding unnecessary token cost.

Restructuring the application to send the persona and rules once as a system message, with only the actual changing question as the user message, reduces token usage significantly and makes the standing rules easier to update in exactly one place going forward.
Common Mistakes

items: Repeating persistent behavior rules inside every user message instead of placing them once in the system prompt
Putting a one time specific request into the system prompt where it inappropriately persists across the whole conversation
Writing an overly vague system prompt that leaves too much of the model behavior undefined
Assuming a system prompt is an absolute, unbreakable security boundary rather than a strong but not perfect behavioral signal

blocks.text: Practice

Take a prompt you have written that mixes persona instructions with a specific request in one block, split it into a system prompt carrying the persistent behavior and a user prompt carrying only the specific request, and note how much shorter each individual user turn becomes.
Key Takeaway

A system prompt sets persistent behavior, persona, and rules that apply across an entire conversation, a user prompt carries the specific, changing request for each individual turn, and separating these correctly makes an application both more efficient and easier to maintain than treating every prompt as one undifferentiated block.
